problem: The retained donor already contained steering search, matched PERMUTED/random controls and a five-condition causal-family identity gate, but no single provider-independent orchestration primitive bound the required BASELINE_CLEAN, BASELINE_CORRUPTED, INTERVENTION_TARGET, SHAM_CONTROL and OFF_TARGET_CONTROL plan to executor-returned identities before the existing identity gate. This left future local backends to hand-roll condition ordering and plan-vs-observation binding.
hypothesis: A small callback-based orchestrator that canonicalizes the five-condition plan before execution and checks returned condition/family/generation/input/intervention identity before delegating to the existing family identity gate will reduce relabeling and cross-control integration risk without creating a second J-Space wire or execution authority.
counterhypothesis: The identity gate alone is sufficient because a backend can construct five trial objects directly. This is rejected as an integration strategy because it does not bind a predeclared plan to each actual callback invocation and therefore permits backend-specific orchestration drift outside the shared primitive.

semantics: delegation to existing model/runtime/loader/trace/output family identity gate
